skill.name: pr-to-video
skill.description: Create a developer-facing video from a GitHub pull request by fetching PR facts, planning a storyboard, building HyperFrames frames, adding audio and captions, and rendering an MP4.
skill.summary: Turns a GitHub pull request into a narrated code-change explainer video.
skill.author: heygen-com

security_audit.summary: The static scan contains many false positives from Markdown backticks, JavaScript template literals, and regular-expression exec calls. Confirmed risk remains from intended local execution, filesystem writes, credentialed GitHub and HeyGen workflows, external network dependencies, and an initialization step that can update global skills from GitHub.

remediation.issue: Unpinned global skill updates during initialization
remediation.suggestion: Pin HyperFrames and skill versions, and require explicit user confirmation before updating any global skill set from GitHub.

remediation.issue: External command execution through gh, node, npx, and the audio engine
remediation.suggestion: Document the command allowlist, validate PR references and engine paths, and reject untrusted HF_MEDIA_ENGINE values outside approved directories.
Warn users before processing private repositories, keep credentials out of project files, and provide a cleanup step for capture/pr.json and capture/diff.patch.

remediation.issue: Filesystem writes are controlled by project path arguments
remediation.suggestion: Constrain --hyperframes, --out-dir, and related output paths to the intended project root and reject traversal or absolute paths when not required.

remediation.issue: External CDN and font dependencies in generated HTML
remediation.suggestion: Vendor or pin GSAP and font assets where possible, or clearly disclose that preview and render may contact external providers.

semantic_findings.title: Credentialed GitHub PR Data Export
semantic_findings.description: fetch-pr.mjs runs the GitHub CLI with local credentials and writes PR metadata and diff content into capture files. Private PR contents can therefore persist on disk in the generated video project.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script directly executes gh and writes pr.json plus diff.patch. This is intended functionality, but it creates a clear data-handling risk for private repositories.

semantic_findings.title: Avatar Fetch Uses Mutable URL Input
semantic_findings.description: fetch-people-avatars.mjs reads avatarUrl from people.json and fetches it without enforcing a GitHub-only host. If that project file is modified, the script can request arbitrary URLs and write the response into assets.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The normal ingest path creates GitHub avatar URLs, but the fetch script trusts the persisted JSON value. The risk depends on project-file tampering, so confidence is medium-high rather than absolute.

content.value_statement: Pull requests are hard to explain across code, behavior, and impact. This skill turns PR facts into a narrated HyperFrames video workflow.
actual_capabilities: Fetches pull request metadata, files, and diffs through the GitHub CLI.
Creates a storyboard and narration plan for a code-change explainer.
Builds a Claude-style HyperFrames design system and frame plan.
Coordinates narration, captions, background music, and sound effects.
Assembles, validates, previews, and renders the final MP4 video.
limitations: Requires GitHub CLI access to the target pull request.
Runs local Node scripts, npx commands, and network requests.
Does not capture websites or create product launch videos.
Needs user approval before storyboard approval and final render.

use_cases.title: Explain a complex code review
use_cases.description: Create a short walkthrough that shows the important diff, behavior change, and impact before review.

use_cases.title: Share a release change
use_cases.description: Turn a merged PR into a concise changelog video for sprint reviews or stakeholder updates.

use_cases.title: Show a technical feature
use_cases.description: Produce a developer-facing feature explainer grounded in the actual pull request and code changes.

prompt_templates.title: Start with defaults
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a pull request explainer video for this PR: <PR URL>. Use the recommended length and ask me before rendering.

prompt_templates.title: Make a fix explainer
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn <owner>/<repo>#<number> into a 60 second fix explainer for developers. Highlight the bug, the fix, and the result.

prompt_templates.title: Build a refactor walkthrough
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a refactor walkthrough from this PR. Show the old shape, the new structure, and one mechanism frame that proves behavior stays stable.

prompt_templates.title: Produce a release-ready video
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a polished changelog video for this PR in landscape format. Include code beats, a mechanism beat, captions, music, and a final MP4.

output_examples.input: A small bugfix PR with one focused diff and default settings.
output_examples.output: A 30 to 45 second fix explainer with a problem hook, before-after code beat, impact frame, captions, and MP4 render.

output_examples.input: A feature PR with several changed files and reviewer activity.
output_examples.output: A 60 to 90 second feature reveal with selected code hunks, an animated behavior diagram, optional contributor close, and review preview.

output_examples.input: A large release PR that groups several related changes.
output_examples.output: A concise changelog video that compresses related changes into three clear beats and avoids reading the diff file by file.

best_practices: Confirm the PR route, audience, aspect ratio, language, and target length before setup.
Keep the video focused on two to four meaningful code or behavior beats.
Review the storyboard before audio, frame generation, and final rendering.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for website capture, product launch promos, or topic explainers without a PR.
Do not narrate every changed file or commit in order.
Do not run it against private PRs without confirming local storage and credential use.

faq.question: What input does this skill need?
faq.answer: It needs a GitHub pull request URL, an owner/repo reference, or a checked-out repository with a current PR.

faq.question: Does it capture the product website?
faq.answer: No. It reads PR data through the GitHub CLI and builds invented visuals, code frames, captions, and audio.

faq.question: Can it work with private repositories?
faq.answer: Yes, if the local GitHub CLI can access the PR. Private PR data may be written into the project folder.

faq.question: Does it require HeyGen credentials?
faq.answer: HeyGen credentials are used for online voice, music, and sound workflows. The skill can continue offline when configured to do so.

faq.question: What file does it produce?
faq.answer: The workflow renders a final MP4 under the project renders folder after validation and user approval.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
